boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: No-admission activities on campus and in nearby Scranton with current public evidence of free access.

cards.title: Swim at Connell Park Pool
cards.subtitle: Scranton Parks & Recreation • 800 Gibbons Street
cards.notes: Bring a swimsuit and meet friends during the posted outdoor-pool window; the city lists this pool as free and open to the public.
cards.short_summary: A city-operated outdoor pool with no admission fee.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Scranton lists Connell Park Pool among its outdoor pools and splash pads that are free and open to the public, with no admission fee required.
cards.source_title: Parks and Recreation — City of Scranton
cards.access_notes: The city posts Connell Park Pool at 800 Gibbons Street and lists outdoor-pool hours as 12–6 p.m., seven days a week; confirm seasonal operation before going.

cards.title: Swim at Nay Aug Park Pool
cards.subtitle: Nay Aug Park • 400 Arthur Avenue
cards.notes: Plan a daylight pool hang at Nay Aug with friends; the city identifies the outdoor activity pool as free public access.
cards.short_summary: A free outdoor pool inside Scranton’s largest park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Scranton lists Nay Aug Park Pool as a free outdoor pool open to the public with no admission fee required.
cards.source_title: Parks and Recreation — City of Scranton
cards.access_notes: Listed at 400 Arthur Avenue with 12–6 p.m. hours, seven days a week, and accessible walk/roll-in entry; availability is seasonal.

cards.title: Cool off at Novembrino Splash Pad
cards.subtitle: Novembrino Park • 200 10th Avenue
cards.notes: Use this as a low-key warm-weather meetup; check the city page before heading out because its status is listed as coming soon.
cards.short_summary: A public splash pad planned for free use.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Scranton states that its outdoor pools and splash pads are free and open to the public with no admission fee required, and lists Novembrino Splash Pad at 200 10th Avenue.
cards.source_title: Parks and Recreation — City of Scranton
cards.access_notes: The city lists Novembrino Splash Pad as “Coming Soon”; verify that it has opened before making plans.

cards.title: Meet at Weston Field House Outdoor Pool
cards.subtitle: Weston Field House • 982 Providence Road
cards.notes: Gather for a summer swim at the outdoor activity pool, not the separate indoor pool that has an admission charge.
cards.short_summary: A free outdoor pool with accessible walk/roll-in entry.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Scranton lists the Weston Field House outdoor pool among outdoor pools that are free and open to the public with no admission fee required.
cards.source_title: Parks and Recreation — City of Scranton
cards.access_notes: Use the outdoor pool listing at 982 Providence Road; the city separately says its indoor pool charges admission. Outdoor hours are listed as 12–6 p.m., seven days a week.

cards.title: Bring a game to Dionne Green
cards.subtitle: University of Scranton lawn and amphitheater
cards.notes: Bring a ball, cards, or a blanket and use the open lawn for a casual group break; keep setups simple and follow campus rules.
cards.short_summary: Campus lawn space designated for free play.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Scranton’s Dionne Green facility page lists “Free play” among the recommended uses for its lawn and amphitheater.
cards.source_title: Dionne Green — University of Scranton Reservations
cards.access_notes: For organized setups, consult the University’s reservation procedure; the facility page notes that tents and anything staked into the ground need approval.

cards.title: See an exhibition at Hope Horn Gallery
cards.subtitle: Hyland Hall, fourth floor • Linden Street at Jefferson Avenue
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition, then meet during gallery hours to look closely and discuss a few pieces together without buying anything.
cards.short_summary: Campus gallery exhibitions and lectures are free to the public.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hope Horn Gallery states that all exhibitions and lectures are open to the public free of charge.
cards.source_title: About the Gallery — Hope Horn Gallery
cards.access_notes: The gallery lists hours Sunday–Friday, 12–4 p.m., plus Wednesday 6–8 p.m.; verify the exhibition schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Use the Pro Deo Room guest computers
cards.subtitle: Weinberg Memorial Library, first floor
cards.notes: If you are working with a non-Scranton friend, register at Library Services and use the designated guest computers for research or study.
cards.short_summary: Free public computer access in a named library room.
cards.evidence_claim: Weinberg Memorial Library provides public computer access free of charge and locates its designated guest computers in the first-floor Pro Deo Room.
cards.source_title: Computing and Equipment Use Policies — Weinberg Memorial Library
cards.access_notes: Guests register annually at the Library Services Desk and may use guest computers up to two hours per day during regular library hours.

cards.title: Walk First Friday Scranton
cards.subtitle: Downtown Scranton • first Friday of each month
cards.notes: Meet downtown after 5 p.m., follow the event map, and browse the participating galleries and businesses at your own pace.
cards.short_summary: A recurring downtown art walk with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The University’s community-events page describes First Friday Scranton as a free art walk held on the first Friday of every month at dozens of downtown galleries and businesses.
cards.source_title: Scranton Area Events — University of Scranton Community Relations
cards.access_notes: It is a recurring monthly event; consult First Friday’s current map and participating-venue information before leaving campus.

cards.title: Catch an eligible free Performance Music concert
cards.subtitle: Mulberry Street at Jefferson Avenue
cards.notes: Review the Performance Music listing, choose a concert marked free, and arrive early if seating is first-come, first-seated.
cards.short_summary: A campus performance venue where listed concerts can be admission-free.
cards.evidence_claim: University Performance Music information states that events at the Houlihan-McLean Center are free of admission charge unless otherwise noted.
cards.source_title: University News Index — University of Scranton
cards.access_notes: Only attend events explicitly listed as free; some programs may be excepted or require first-come seating.

cards.entity_name: Weinberg Memorial Library Board Game Collection
cards.title: Play a library board game
cards.subtitle: Weinberg Memorial Library • Reilly Learning Commons, Pro Deo Room, or Media Lounge
cards.notes: Choose a game from the library collection and play it in one of the named campus rooms; ask Library Services about current availability.
cards.short_summary: Library games can be played on site in designated rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Weinberg Memorial Library reports that its board-game collection can be played in the Reilly Learning Commons, Pro Deo Room, and Media Lounge.
cards.access_notes: The library says games are also available for five-day checkout; confirm the collection and room availability with Library Services.
